narrative.overview:
The site is the couple's printed invitation unfolded into one long sheet. Everything it is made of comes from that card: the four-colour palette, the mandala lattice, the flower corners and crown, the dark blue rule, the formal script for the names and the bookish serif for everything else. It is warm, ceremonial and unhurried, with the composure of stationery rather than the density of an interface.

Cream paper carries the framed moments. Between them, whole fields of pink, dark blue and yellow arrive edge to edge, so colour reads as a change of sheet instead of an accent. Facts stay plain and softly sized: a date, a time and a venue are set like the lines of a card, with their actions directly beneath. The whole type scale sits small for a softer, more elegant feel.

Motion behaves like the object it describes. The monogram traces itself, the card parts like two doors, script headings wipe on as if written, the prints drift slightly with the scroll, and the hero photograph leans toward the pointer. All of it falls away under reduced motion.
keyCharacteristics: One palette of four invitation colours plus a single deepened blue for legibility.
Rule frames with the invitation's flower corners, scaled and positioned by one measure.
A mandala lattice at 12%, behind cream and pink only.
Vienna Romance for names and headings; Libre Baskerville in caps, italic and regular for the rest.
A small, soft type scale: body at 0.9375rem, the smallest type at 0.625rem.
Square paper, soft shadows only under objects that are physically paper.

rules.name: The Large Pink Rule
rules.body: Pink text stays at 24px (1.5rem) or larger, because of contrast (3.30:1 on cream, 2.06:1 on dark blue). Below that size pink is ornament only: the monogram, the flower art, the date row's diamond. In the build pink on dark blue appears only as ornament; at 2.06:1 it does not reach 3:1 even for large type, so treat ornament as its practical limit there.

rules.name: The Small Text Rule
rules.body: Small text is dark blue on cream, cream on dark blue, or Deep Ink Blue (#2f3b43) on yellow. Dark blue on yellow measures 4.19:1 and is why the deepened blue exists; Deep Ink Blue on yellow measures 6.85:1.

rules.name: The Large Field Text Rule
rules.body: Cream on pink (3.30:1) and yellow on dark blue (4.19:1) are for large type only: the bridge statement and the closing ampersand.

rules.name: The Whole Field Rule
rules.body: Colour arrives as whole full-bleed sections that meet on a hard edge. A section is cream, pink, dark blue or yellow, and its type follows the pairings above.

rules.name: The Twelve Percent Rule
rules.body: The lattice is `pattern.png` at 12% opacity, centred from the top and tiled at max(62rem, 100%) wide. It appears only behind cream or pink, never dark blue or yellow. It keeps its own pink and yellow on cream and is filtered to white on pink. Framed sheets sit on solid cream above it.

rules.name: The Soft Scale Rule
rules.body: The whole scale stays small for a softer, more elegant feel, with body at 0.9375rem and nothing below 0.625rem. Hierarchy comes from the script and from a change of cut, not from sheer size.

rules.name: The Script Is For Names Rule
rules.body: Vienna Romance sets names and headings only, with a hairline stroke of 0.012em in the text colour so its thin strokes hold on screen. Anything a guest must read to act is in Libre Baskerville.

rules.name: The Three Cuts Rule
rules.body: Libre Baskerville appears in regular, italic and uppercase with tracking, all at weight 400. Emphasis comes from size, italic or a change of field, not from bold.

rules.name: The Caps Carry Facts Rule
rules.body: Tracked capitals carry dates, event labels and the invitation's own words. They never become an invented label above a heading.

rules.name: The Logistics In Reach Rule
rules.body: Date, time, venue, directions and calendar sit together in one block, so nothing a guest needs is more than a tap away.

rules.name: The Paper Lifts Rule
rules.body: Only objects that would be physical paper carry a shadow, and only those objects tilt (between 1.5deg and 5deg, easing toward level on hover). The hero's stack of prints may also lean in perspective toward the pointer, up to 3.5deg on each axis. Fields, frames, sheets and buttons stay flat.

rules.name: The Landing Rule
rules.body: Flower corners use offsets proportional to the corner measure (top −0.033, bottom −0.008, sides −0.03) so the rule drawn in the artwork lands on the CSS frame line at every size. When a frame changes its corner measure, it inherits these ratios unchanged, and the frame's border thickness is derived from the same measure.

rules.name: The Small Crown Rule
rules.body: The crown is only ever small (3.5rem), whatever it heads. On the reception and footer, where no frame carries it, it sits centred on the seam with the section above.

dos: Do set small text as dark blue on cream, cream on dark blue, or Deep Ink Blue (#2f3b43) on yellow.
Do keep the lattice to `pattern.png` at 12%, behind cream or pink only, filtered white on pink.
Do position flower corners with offsets proportional to the corner measure, so the rule in the artwork lands on the CSS frame line.
Do derive frame border thickness from the same corner measure: max(1.5px, corner × 0.009).
Do give colour to whole sections and let them meet on a hard edge.
Do keep the crown at 3.5rem, and centre it on the seam where no frame carries it.
Do keep touch targets at 2.75rem or larger and retain the 2px current-colour focus outline.
Do make every motion optional under reduced motion, leaving the page fully readable, and keep the hero's pointer tilt to hover-capable devices.
donts: Don't set pink text below 24px, or use pink for text on dark blue; below that size it is ornament only.
Don't set small text in dark blue directly on yellow; use Deep Ink Blue.
Don't set the lattice outside the invitation's 10% to 15% range.
Don't put the lattice behind dark blue or yellow.
Don't position a flower corner with fixed offsets, or change its aspect ratio without redrawing the offsets.
Don't set Vienna Romance for dates, times, venues or actions.
Don't use bold; Libre Baskerville stays at weight 400.
Don't add a small capitalised label above a heading unless it is the invitation's own wording.
Don't add shadow or tilt to fields, frames, sheets or buttons.
Don't round frames, buttons or photographs; the circle is reserved for icon-only controls.
